query: Can we exploit RDD around eligibility thresholds to strengthen identification, and how should we choose bandwidths and covariates for local IV designs?

response.query: Can we exploit RDD around eligibility thresholds to strengthen identification, and how should we choose bandwidths and covariates for local IV designs?
response.answer: Exploiting RDD around eligibility thresholds strengthens identification by isolating causal effects. Choose bandwidths based on local variation and covariates based on potential confounders. Use sensitivity analysis to assess robustness.

results.title: [PDF] Thesis - UvA-DARE (Digital Academic Repository)
results.content: An “Excellence in Knowledge Sharing” award is presented at the company’s annual meeting to encourage managers to share innovations in their unit with managers of other units. Royal Alberta wants its managers to share knowledge and cooperate with other managers in the company. Thus, sharing knowledge about the quick delivery system may negatively affect the financial performance and rank of your unit. The study examines whether and how the source of knowledge and the presence of status incentives affect business unit managers’ knowledge transfer decisions in multi-unit firms. It disentangles how sourcing knowledge internally or externally may affect managers’ sense of psychological ownership of the knowledge in their business unit. However, when firms offer status recognition for knowledge transfer, managers’ willingness to transfer knowledge to other business units increases for both internal and external knowledge. Ik kijk of de bron van kennis, intern of extern, van invloed is op het gevoel van psychologisch eigenaarschap van managers over de kennis in hun business unit.
